15 Years of Stimulus, and Nothing to Show
Related, see http://www.shadowstats.com/, or a short interview with the author (David Stockman) here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p0YNc5S7XtQ&feature=youtu.be

Somewhat interesting, but I notice there aren't any charts actually talking about the "stimulus" of the last 15 years. What counts as stimulus, and how does it compare to the previous time periods? This whole post is about proving how bad the last 15 years were, but I doubt anyone would seriously oppose that viewpoint. The question we are debating is why?

Some points: what about rising healthcare costs? Healthcare is usually given as part of your income from your employer. Rising healthcare costs should cut into the rate of increase of disposable income, even if total compensation is rising at the same rate as before healthcare costs were growing. Could that help explain some of these phenomenon?

With the flatlining of hours worked, is that necessarily a bad thing? It seems like that standard of living today is better than 15 years ago, but our population is much higher and we did all that with the same amount of hours worked? Doesn't that equate to more leisure time? Could be a good thing. Moreover, total hours worked has definitely dropped due to baby boomers retiring. The huge amount of children born between 1945-1950 are now 65-70 years old now. Prime retirement age. Combined with the economic downturn, hours worked isn't nearly as "bad" as it looks.

Also, why is he concerned specifically about manufacturing jobs? Shouldn't the market determine what jobs people should have? If our talents can be spent more efficiently on service jobs, that's not an inherently bad thing.

Hey whats up! I found this subverse and I thought, why not share some of my own advice that helped me on my journey to sculpting my dream physique. While I am still in the process, I did have to overcome many hurdles to get where I am now. So here I go:

Getting Started Just trying to fathom the initial confidence and energy is definitely the hardest part, but PLEASE don't let this discourage you from starting. I have been getting active and going to the gym everyday for about 7-months now but it was not easy when I first started. First let me begin by disclaiming that I am by no means fat whatsoever. I am 21 and currently weigh 165 lbs. However, before I began working out I picked up the horrible habit of smoking cigarettes and drinking everyday. This was mostly because my roommate was a heavy smoker and drinker, and since I was around him all the time I picked up on his habits. So when I decided to finally hit the gym for the first time in a while, I was in horrible condition. My breathing was terrible. I would become light headed and nearly passed out multiple times. Also I would see other gym goers who have been working out for much longer than I, and seeing their bodies made me feel insecure. After my first day I was sure I would give up, but then I thought about all the negatives of my body now and realized there is only one way to cure my bad habits... and that was to stay committed and fight against the awful temptations that got me in this mess in the first place. The next day I went to the gym I had a totally different attitude. When I engaged my workouts I paced myself so not to push myself beyond anything I wasn't capable of doing, and I paid attention only to myself and no one else. I knew that comparing myself with people who have been in the gym longer than I, made no sense and only inhibited me mentally. To help myself I isolated myself in different areas of the gym for different workouts, kept my headphones in, and only focused on me!

Research So before even going to the gym it is normal to look up some workouts online for you to do. But after the first week and a half of working out I felt like I was getting nowhere. I would do a montage of workouts but I felt like I was just going in circles. I just felt like I wasn't getting anything significant done. It wasn't until then, that I went online and did further research on how to construct a proper workout regimen. However, while doing this research I learned that working to getting that perfect bod could not be attained by just physical activity. Other important factors such as dieting, stretching, cardio, and rest was crucial. Doing more and more research I learned so much about my body and what it takes to maintain superior health. This is something I can't stress enough. DO RESEARCH! Learn about your body, what type of body you have, measure your fat percentage, etc. When you become more familiar with yourself, you will feel this connection with your body that you probably haven't had before. Now I know it sounds weird, but I can't make this up. You just have to take my word that this is something that exists and when you find it you will feel so different.

Lifestyle So after about a month I was comfortable walking into the gym with no problem. I felt like a regular and accepted that this is something I'm not new to anymore. I wasn't like one of the athletic gym members but I was someone who took time out of my day to better myself, and knowing that felt great. It was at this point I realized how far I've come and how much I've changed, not physically but as a person entirely. I was eating much healthier foods and keeping track of how much I ate, making sure I didn't eat too much nor too little. I made sure that I got proper rest everyday and I began every morning with stretches and a mile jog. Going to the gym and making all these changes was more than something I needed to do but it became something that I wanted to do. I realized that this was a lifestyle. This is so important. When you decide to take on this journey, understand that this is a life choice. This is your choice to shape your body and mind for a healthier alternative. Once I reached this point I never wanted to go back. My roommate would offer a smoke and drink but I was surprised and proud to see that I would decline these temptations without effort. When you get here it feels so great! I encourage you to strive and don't give up until you reach this place of serenity; where temptation can no longer phase you (if that is your struggle).

Summary So as I'm sure you have heard a million times, this type of lifestyle is a commitment. You really have to push yourself and you can't expect it to be something easy. You will not see results in a one day or a week. You need to give the process time. You need to give your body time to react and break itself in to your new routine. I can tell you now that after about 3-4 weeks you will feel results. Your routine will only get easier and easier the more you keep on going out and getting active. Do not be someone who gives in easily. Fight for it! Also don't feel insecure when you begin either. You have to come to acceptance of your current physical state and be conscious that you need to make this change. Strengthen your mental state first so you can strengthen the physical. This is the only way you will stay committed. This is really an internal battle with yourself to see if you are capable of making a significant change for the better. If you ever feel like giving up, do whatever it takes to overcome that feeling of doubt! Look up inspiring videos, change your phone screen background to your dream body, whatever! Just make sure you NEVER GIVE UP! Also when you engage in your workouts DO NOT half ass it! Push yourself! Get sweaty! Feel pain! Feel the burn! Whenever physical pain overcame me, I would recite the popular marine quote, "Pain is only weakness leaving the body." And this is true! As I said before, the more you keep going to the gym and taking on these activities, they will only get easier for you!

To wrap up I thought why not tell you my weekly workout routine. Im not going to tell you specific workouts, but rather share with you different muscle groups to engage by day when you go to the gym as well as things to do before your workout.

Pre-Workout Everyday - Stretch your entire body (head to toe) - Jog (set a distance or a time limit; maybe you can throw in some interval sprints)

Weekly Muscle Group Workout * Monday - Chest; Shoulders; Triceps * Tuesday - Back (upper & lower); Quadriceps (Squats); Biceps * Wednesday - Leg Day! :D (Quads, Hamstrings, Calves, Hip-flexers) * Thursday - Chest; Shoulders; Triceps; Quadriceps (Squats) * Friday - Back (Upper & Lower); Biceps * Saturday - REST! * Sunday - REST!

Post-Workout * Core (Planks & Other core workouts) * Jog (Set a distance or time limit)

Workout Explained - The workout routine is quite basic but I found it to be very effective in both building strength and burning fat. What Id like you to take note of is how I engage legs 3-times a week instead of just having one day dedicated to legs. This is because in my research I found people that only do legs once a week aren't optimizing their overall body strength. Understand that there are two halves to your body. Upper and lower. Both halves coincide with each other, so doing one more than the other is counterproductive to overall body functionality and strength. Imo I find legs to be the most important part of the body to look after anyway.

  • While you will be burning fat by engaging those muscles in your workout, I found that I shredded most of my fat from core workouts and running. Just about any workout you do engages your core so you really don't want to leave it out during the week. But you also do not want to over work your core either, let alone any part of your body. Also I have running at the beginning and end of my workouts. I find running before you workout to be beneficial because it heats up your body, preparing you for a serious workout and to get you to sweat during the entire workout. From what I've researched I found that running after your workout is very important because running releases lactic acid from your muscles, which builds up while you workout. Releasing lactic acid by running is supposed to help prevent your muscles from becoming sore and achy after a workout.

Hopefully, you guys were able to make it through this whole post! I really hope I was helpful and encouraged you to take that first step towards a healthy lifestyle! Good luck and if you have any questions I'd be more than happy to answer any!

Have a wonderful day :)
